transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I really hope I'm not wasting your time here. 

I guess... well, I'm a construction manager, and I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. I try really hard to do a good job, I promise I do. But, like, I can start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, and I'm really trying hard to pay attention. But within just a few minutes, my mind is already off on, you know, three other job problems. And then I end up missing things I know I should have caught. 

It's pretty embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I know better. Does... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up?
Did you struggle with these kinds of attention and focus difficulties when you were a child or in school?

Um, well... yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker, because I always wanted to do the right thing and make my teachers happy. But, um... back in elementary school, I guess they were already telling my parents that I had some... well, a lot of extra energy. 

They said I couldn't really stay in my seat, and I'd accidentally talk out of turn sometimes. Just getting a little too eager, maybe? And I'd end up losing my homework, or I'd rush through the directions on assignments before I actually understood what I was supposed to be doing. I always felt awful when they had to correct me. 

Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information here.
Nowadays, do you still feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still or feel an internal need to always be on the go?

Um, well... I guess I do like to keep busy. I really try to be respectful during our site meetings, I swear I do. But... well, in meetings where everybody else can just sit quietly through the whole thing, I'm usually the guy who ends up standing up in the back. 

Or I'll, you know, walk over to get some coffee, or step outside just to check on something real quick... basically just making a little excuse to move around. I really don't mean to be disruptive to the team, it's just... sitting in one chair for that long feels really, really tough for me. I try to hold it in, but I just get this urge to be on my feet. 

I hope that doesn't sound too unprofessional. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
